newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Key advisor says dissidents behind Indonesia riots.
newsitem.headline: Key advisor says dissidents behind Indonesia riots.

text.p: A senior advisor to Indonesian President Suharto has accused unnamed dissidents of inciting recent social disturbances and riots, the Jakarta Post newspaper reported on Thursday.
Sudomo, chairman of the Supreme Advisory Council, was quoted as blaming the unrest on dissidents unhappy with the nation's development.

"They (dissidents) will incite people to commit violence, manipulating sensitive issues such as differences in religion, ethnic groups and social and cultural conditions," he told reporters on Wednesday.

The retired admiral rejected suggestions by political analysts and sociologists that the riots were caused by social and economic gaps between the rich and poor among Indonesia's population of almost 200 million people.
Sudomo, head of the powerful national security agency Kopkamtib in the 1980s, did not name the dissidents. Officials at the advisory board were not available for comment on Thursday.

Four people died after an angry mob went on the rampage in Tasikmalaya, West Java, in December, setting fire to shops, buildings and churches. The violence was apparently sparked by reports of police brutality towards a Moslem religious teacher.

Sudomo said the riots were not caused by social and economic gaps. "It's not true the violence was triggered by social and economic gaps. The Tasikmalaya people are a well-paid society," he said. The paper gave no other details.

The Tasikmalaya riot followed a similar incident in Situbondo, East Java, in October when thousands of Moslems burned churches as well as other buildings. Five people died in the riot, sparked by a court hearing into a case of alleged blasphemy against Islam.

Last year, Jakarta suffered the worst riots in more than twenty years, after police raided the headquarters of the Indonesian Democratic Party (PDI) on July 27. Supporters of opposition figure Megawati Sukarnoputri were taken into custody after the police raid.
